title: Chick Webb at Connie's Inn and tap dancers' night
summary: The first big band they appeared with was Chick Webb at Connie's Inn during Bubbles' second illness; Friday dancers' night used a searchlight to pick who danced the Shim Sham Shimmy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So, now, the first big band for you to appear with was who?
The first big band we appeared with was actually Chick Webb.
This was prior to Louis Armstrong or --
Uh-huh. Why don't you tell me a little bit about that?

Well, it was during the second illness of John Bubbles, see. He was living up on Sugar Hill there at Park Fort Lincoln, on Edgecombe Avenue, and he sent us down to Connie's Carny's Inn and Chick Webb was playing there at the time and also a house band. And he hadn't discovered Ella Fitzgerald yet. And we were playing there and we was breaking in a new routine -- a new tap dance, and they used to have tap dancers' night down there on Fridays. They'd have a searching spot light -- a spot light would go searching through the audience and the master of ceremonies, he would be -- already had spoken to the

projectionist -- the light man, electrician, and tell him who's sitting in the audience and where to stop the light. And whoever the light stopped on, they would have to get up and do one chorus of their version of a tap dance they was calling the Shim-Sham Shimmy. It was really from a chorus girl's encore dance. And that's what happened, see. Well, he eventually got -- he overcome -- he overcome the double pneumonia, you see, and -- but we were doing so good then until they decided that we should be an act all of our own, you see. Because the money was better and it would be better if we were out of their act, you know, and doing an act of our own, you see. Like that -- get more money that way.
Talking about the Shim-Sham Shimmy, I'm wondering whether --

That's what it was, you see. But that dance -- it was all right, it really -- sometimes it stopped the shows, you see, because everybody doing it -- their version. They couldn't do it like someone they had seen, they had to do it their own way. They had to originate a way of doing the Shim-Sham Shimmy, you see.
